editorial:
Imagine two chaotic troublemakers getting let out of prison only to end up at a strict Christian TV station. That is exactly what happens to Winnie and Karina. These two girls are far from holy, and they are convinced they are going to make a million kroner just by showing up. The vibe is totally wild because you have these loud, flashy characters crashing into a world of quiet prayers and boring board meetings. It is a classic fish-out-of-water setup where you just know things are going to blow up in the worst way possible.

You will love how the actresses play these roles because they are completely believable as mess-ups. The pacing is quick, and the jokes land well because the clash of personalities is so extreme. While some of the humor is a bit over-the-top, it mostly works to keep you laughing.
endingExplained: In the end, the huge misunderstanding about the million kroner check finally clears up. Winnie and Karina realize they aren't getting rich, but they have already caused total mayhem at the TV station. After all the fighting and loud arguments, they find a way to actually help the channel in their own weird way. They don't suddenly become saints, but they find a spot where they fit in, leaving the warden very happy they are gone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy comedies about people causing trouble.
